title: What is known about 1RB0RF_1LC0RA_1LD1LB_0LE---_1LA0LA_1RE1LD
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0RF_1LC0RA_1LD1LB_0LE---_1LA0LA_1RE1LD.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: Open. The run is a sequence of cycles, from one block of n ones to the next: n = 2, 42, 160, …, 71,144,918 so far (14 cycles, no halt to 2.8·1016 steps). Proved in Lean for every size: the ones become copies of 01, an inner counter eats them from the right (two copies and two ones become three copies, the ones are refilled from the copies), and at the end the copies become ones again. Between those, a cycle may pass through E-phases, in which the same kind of counter runs through a stretch of zeros and spawns sub-counters; that part is not decoded.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (D1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 39,747 cells have been visited and 19,882 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: A block of ones turns into copies of 01
claims.text: For every x: 0^inf C> 1^(2x+2) 0^inf reaches 0^inf D> (01)^(2x+3) 1 0^inf. After a start (c_start, d_first), each round of the sweep runs right over the copies of 01 and back, turns two ones into a copy of 01 and adds one more copy at the left end (d_round), by induction in sweep.

claims.title: Copies of 01 turn back into one block of ones
claims.text: For every x: 0^inf A> 1 1 (01)^x 0^inf reaches 0^inf C> 1^(2x+6) 0^inf in 4x+14 steps, one pass right and one back.

claims.title: The cycles by direct simulation, to step 5.23·10<sup>10</sup>
claims.text: Direct simulation from blank tape passes through C> 1^n (the whole tape one block of ones, head in C at its left end) for n = 2, 42, 160, 412, 1,202, 3,400, 19,880, 95,802, 272,964, each time right after A> 1 1 (01)^m with n = 2m+6, and no halt.

claims.title: The inner counter, exactly
claims.text: After the sweep the tape is 1 (01)^N 0 0, N = n+1, head in F at the right end, and the inner counter starts: X(p, q, r) = 0^inf 1 (01)^p 1 B> 1 (01)^q (11)^r 0^inf, a head block at the right end that eats the copies of 01 on its left. A round takes X(p+2, q, r+1) to X(p, q+3, r) (two copies and two ones become three copies); with no ones left, X(p+1, q, 0) restarts as X(p, 1, q+1). When the copies on the left are used up (p = 0 or 1) the head runs to the left end: A> 0 x (01)^m (11)^s with (x, m, s) = g(N, 1, 0), g a recursion on p. Proved for every N: from C(2x+2) the machine reaches that configuration (fphase); this part of a cycle cannot halt.

claims.title: Rounds of the head block in other surroundings
claims.text: With zeros on its left the head block eats two zeros per round: L 0 0 0 1 B> 1 (01)^q 1 1 R reaches L 0 1 B> 1 (01)^(q+2) R (z_round); with blank tape on its left the tape grows: b_round. And 0^inf 1 (01)^m 0 A> reaches C(2m+4) (to_c).

claims.title: What happens at the left end
claims.text: From A> 0 x (01)^m 1^k (k even): if x = 0 and m is even the inner counter starts again with N = m+k+3; if x = 0 and m is odd an E-phase starts from 1 (01)^(m+2) 0^(k+2) 01 E>; if x = 1 the cycle ends, 1 (01)^(m+k) 0 A> and then C(2(m+k)+4). After an E-phase (k odd or even, x = 1 or none): k even ends the cycle, k odd restarts the counter with N = m+k−1. Checked on all 35 such events of the run to 2.8·1016 steps, and g on all 25 counter starts.

claims.title: 14 cycles, no halt to 2.8·10<sup>16</sup> steps
claims.text: An accelerated simulator (runs of a word crossed at once, and shift rules u^n w → w v^n found and applied automatically; exact, its edge events agree cell for cell with direct simulation for all 56 events to 3·109 steps) passes through C(n) for n = 2, 42, 160, 412, 1,202, 3,400, 19,880, 95,802, 272,964, 823,870, 2,418,210, 8,391,884, 22,740,810, 71,144,918 (the last at step 5.74·1015) and runs to step 2.8·1016 without a halt.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: The inner counter and the outer parts of a cycle are proved and cannot halt; the transitions at the left end are checked on the run. What is left is the E-phase: the head block running through a stretch of zeros, where each run-out of ones plants a new block of copies of 01 inside the zeros, on which a counter of the same kind runs, and so on. It is a recursive counter of the same family, and it is where a halt (D reads 1) could be.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. The tape keeps coming back to a single block of ones, each time longer. This page shows the cycle between two such moments: the two outer parts are proved in Lean for every size, the middle part is a second counter that has not been decoded.

facts.text: No halt in the C simulator; 39,747 cells visited.
No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.
The two outer parts of a cycle, proved for every size.
Proved for every size: no halt there.
14 cycles, no halt to 2.8·10<sup>16</sup> steps (accelerated, exact simulator).

sections.heading: Ones into pairs and back
html: Every so often the whole tape is one block of n ones with the head, in state C, at its left end. Call that C(n). The run from blank passes through C(n) for n = 2, 42, 160, 412, 1,202, 3,400, 19,880, 95,802, 272,964, and the time between two of them grows a little faster than n2. Each stretch between two is a cycle, in three parts.

A copy of 01 is written in front of the block and the head starts a sweep: each round it runs right over all the copies and back, two ones at the left end of the block become a copy of 01, and one more copy is added at the left end of the tape. Proved in Lean for every size:
2. A second counter at the right end (not decoded)

Next a small block of ones appears at the right end of the copies and starts sweeps of its own. In each of them two copies on its left are used up, three copies are added between, and two ones are spent; when the round is over the block comes back about three times longer (2, 18, 54, …). When the copies on the left run out, runs of zeros are left behind, and the process restarts further left. This middle part ends with the head at the left end in state A, on 1 1 (01)^m, for an m that has so far been between 1.3n and 2.9n.
One pass right and one back fill the copies in: A> 1 1 (01)^m  →  C> 1^(2m+6), proved in Lean. That is the next C(n).

The inner counter

Once the ones are copies of 01, a small head block appears at the right end: 1 B> 1 (01)^q (11)^r. Each round it eats two copies of 01 on its left and two of its own ones and grows by three copies: (p, q, r) → (p−2, q+3, r−1). When its ones are gone it turns its q copies into 2q+2 ones and starts again with q = 1, using one more copy on the left. So r goes 2, 8, 26, 80, … (r+1 triples) while the copies on the left are eaten, until fewer than two are left. Then the head runs to the left end, and depending on what is left there the counter starts again, the cycle ends, or an E-phase begins: the same head block now runs through a long stretch of zeros (eating two zeros per round), and every time its ones run out it plants a block of copies of 01 in the zeros, on which a counter of the same kind runs. That nesting is what is not decoded.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.41). Right of the start it stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half).
After 109 steps the tape spans 39,747 cells (28,532 left of the start, 614 right), with a density of 1s of 0.5.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: The middle of a cycle
html: The ratios n′/n (3.8, 2.6, 2.9, 2.8, 5.8, 4.8, 2.8) do not follow an obvious rule, which is what one expects when the second counter's state at the moment the copies run out depends on remainders. Halting is possible only where state D reads a 1. Deciding the machine needs the middle part written as rules, like the two outer parts; until then the question is open.

sections.heading: Related machines
html: Other holdouts of the list of 608 that are tied to this one. The comparison of tables is exact; everything about runs was checked on the first 107 steps of each machine and is an observation, not a proof (holdouts/related.py, holdouts/related.json).

Same table as the machines below, started in another state. Renaming the states as shown turns this machine's table into the other one, the halting transition included. The other machine starts in its own state A, which is not this machine's A: its run from blank tape is the run of this table started in another state. These are different runs: in the first 107 steps of each, no configuration of this machine's run occurs in any of the others, even up to a shift of the tape. So each of these holdouts is its own halting question, and settling one does not settle another.

summary: Cycles from n ones to n' ones (14 cycles, n up to 7.1e7, no halt to 2.8e16 steps); the inner counter is proved in Lean, a recursive E-phase through zeros is not decoded.
family: nested counter: block of ones <-> copies of 01, an inner tripling counter, recursive E-phase
